newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela hails start of economic recovery.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela hails start of economic recovery.

text.p: Venezuela's economic recovery is ahead of target, with economic growth seen contributing to a two percentage point drop in unemployment this year, Trade and Industry Minister Freddy Rojas Parra said.

"We had thought that it would start to happen in the second half of the year because the economy was still assimilating and coping with the impact of adjustments to costs and spending, but it is reacting sooner than we hoped," Rojas told reporters at Miraflores presidential palace.
The Venezuelan economy contracted 1.6 percent last year and Rojas reiterated the government's forecast of a four percent growth rate for 1997.
"The Venezuelan economy is showing signs of recovery in areas of production, industry, construction, small and medium industry and above all in banks, commerce and services," he said.
"Our aim is two points less unemployment for December 31, 1997," he added. Venezuela's official unemployment rate stood at 11.2 percent at the end of 1996.

Leading the recovery was the car industry, which was seen boosting sales by about 60 percent this year from 70,000 units in 1996 to 110,000 units, Rojas said. Vehicle sales for the first four months of 1997 were up 122 percent, according to Venezuelan Automobile Chamber (Cavenez) figures.
Rojas said there had also been an increase in credit demand and that use of industrial installed capacity was moving steadily towards 60 percent from 50 percent.
A recent 70 percent wage rise for public sector workers and further expected pay rises for private sector workers would stimulate demand even more and drive the recovery on.
"It's too early for important growth figures, but there is a significant sign of changes in the tendency," towards growth, Rojas said.
